newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX bull run intact, but breather on the way.
newsitem.headline: German DAX bull run intact, but breather on the way.

text.p: The German DAX share index's greatest bull run in history is set to continue for the time being, technical analysts said on Tuesday, but a healthy consolidation phase is on the cards in the medium term.
There were signs that the IBIS DAX index was catching its breath in afternoon electronic trade. The index fell over one percent during the day, and by late trade was down 33.94 points at 4,366.85.

"I think that we have generally seen a buying panic. Germany is outperforming the MSCI index, all the European indices, and Standard & Poor's at the moment, all of which has to do with the rise of the dollar, which has risen a bit too much at the moment, so we need a small consolidation," said Volker Bien, chartist at BHF Bank in Frankfurt.
"I think the DAX will build up a bit of support around 4,000 points with relatively little difficulty," said Bien.
Ingo Mainert, Commerzbank chartist, said a consolidation is on the way, but the upward gradient which has seen the DAX rise more than 50 percent this year remains intact.

"The trend that we have seen so far remains intact. Looking at momentum and trend-mapping indicators, there are no signs that the trend will change dramatically. There are technical signs that the market is extremely overbought," said Mainert.

"The deviation of more than 10 percent from the 38-day moving average line is historically very high, which shows the market has advanced very strongly and is on the verge of a consolidation," Mainert said.

In such a volatile environment, even technical analysts are forced to keep an eye on fundamental factors. 4,400 points, a level which the DAX penetrated in recent weeks, could be an important area of resistance.

"We have had high volumes and high volatility. However, we saw that there were no follow-up orders above the 4,440 level. With such high volumes and volatility, then a certain vulnerability enters the market," said Bien.

"We have seen the market topping around 4,440, and at this level talk of dollar pessimism does not apply, talking of pessimism on the DAX or on the Dow Jones is also inappropriate -- we have caution in all the main sectors, which can lead to weakness," he added.
Certain large incidents on the fundamental side, notably the appreciation of the dollar against the mark, have had a big impact on technical analysis.
Another big event was the announcement last Monday that Vereinsbank and Hypo-Bank planned to merge.

Mainert said: "Because of the overbought situation in the market we could see a consolidation in the next four to six weeks, but we could also see the holes in the market, which were brought about by events such as the banking sector merger stories -- these holes could be filled".
For example, the gaps in the charts between 4,250 and 4,210 could be filled in the next two to four weeks, Mainert said.
Generally the market is healthier than the record rises of late would lead one to expect.
"The market is not extremely optimistic. The put/call ratio has come down in recent days, but is generally neutral and there is no extremely high optimism," Mainert said.

Volker Bien said: "I compared a graph of the U.S. share market and the German DAX index when the DAX was around 3,000 points, and this seemed to indicate that Germany would rise very strongly, even though everyone laughed at the comparison. Now we are at 4,500 points and no-one is laughing," said Bien.
"We need a little bit of consolidation because things have gone a bit too far. When we have the correction behind us, then I am sure that technical indicators will issue buy signals," said Bien.
